speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe your wrist pain in detail: when did it start, is it constant or intermittent, and does it radiate? Also, can you describe the skin lesions on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history is concerning for disseminated infection or reactive arthritis; were the skin lesions tender or ulcerated, and do you have any eye or genital symptoms? Also, could you describe the appearance of the lesions on your wrists?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ecthyma gangrenosum (Pseudomonas sepsis) secondary to disseminated infection.

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential, Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_photo_of_wrist_lesions.
